reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Expert witness standards in bench, family, juvenile, and probate proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Governs expert opinion testimony, reasonably relied upon data, ultimate issues, and hypothetical question rules in non-jury actions.

headings.title: Expert witness admissibility standards in other civil and criminal actions
headings.reviewNote: Applies reliability, sufficient-facts, disclosure, and ultimate-issue standards to all actions outside subsection 1, barring criminal mental-state element opinions.

headings.title: Landowner testimony on reasonable market value of property
headings.reviewNote: Preserves common law right of property owners to testify regarding reasonable market value of their land.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections and McDonagh (123 S.W.3d 146) annotation; refined subsection 2 title/note to match statutory scope ("all actions except subsection 1") without extratextual case names.

headings.title: Certified copies of corporate records received as prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Makes certified copies of corporate records attested under seal by secretary or president prima facie evidence.

headings.title: Depository financial institution duplication and check record retention
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes financial institutions to provide record copies complying with section 362.413 check retention requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and corporate-evidence cross-references on certified corporate records and financial institution check/draft duplications under section 362.413.

headings.title: Applicability of service charge affidavits to civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Applies service charge reasonableness and necessity affidavit provisions to civil actions filed in any Missouri court.

headings.title: Affidavit of reasonable and necessary service charges as sufficient evidence
headings.reviewNote: Provides that service charge affidavits support findings of reasonable and necessary charges absent counteraffidavit.

headings.title: Requirements for executing service charge reasonableness affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Specifies affidavit requirements, including execution under oath by service provider and itemized statement.

headings.title: Thirty-day pre-trial filing and service deadline for affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing and service of service charge affidavits on all parties at least thirty days before trial.

headings.title: Deadlines and leave of court for filing controverting counteraffidavits
headings.reviewNote: Establishes deadlines for counteraffidavits within thirty days of receipt and fourteen days before trial, or with leave.

headings.title: Notice requirements and expert qualifications for counteraffiants
headings.reviewNote: Requires counteraffidavits to state grounds under oath and be made by qualified experts in the field.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections on service charge reasonableness/necessity affidavits and counteraffidavits; removed extratextual "medical" from subsection 1 title.

headings.title: Business records affidavit procedure for electronic and reproduced media
headings.reviewNote: Makes durable reproductions admissible as business records upon custodian affidavit meeting section 490.680.

headings.title: Seven-day pre-trial service requirement for business records affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving copies of business records and affidavits on all parties at least seven days prior to trial.

headings.title: Statutory form of business records custodian affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Sets standard statutory form for business records custodian affidavit establishing regularity and timing of records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections, embedded custodian affidavit form, section 362.413 cross-reference, and Russell (35 S.W.3d 507) annotation.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of advance damage payments as admissions of liability
headings.reviewNote: Bars advance accommodation payments for medical expenses or lost earnings from admission as evidence of tort liability.

headings.title: Credit and deduction of advance payments from final settlement or judgment
headings.reviewNote: Credits advance payments against final judgments, prohibiting disclosure of payments to juries at trial.

headings.title: Non-recovery of advance payments upon judgment of non-liability
headings.reviewNote: Bars payors or insurers from suing to recover advance payments if final judgment finds no liability.

headings.title: Statute of limitations tolling until date of last advance payment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that applicable statute of limitations commences on the date of the last advance payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and Taylor/Rook annotations on inadmissibility of advance tort payments, judgment credits, non-recovery, and limitations commencement.

headings.title: Exclusivity of statutory collateral source evidence provisions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts admissibility of collateral source evidence exclusively to provisions set forth in section.

headings.title: Pre-trial special damage payments by defendant non-recoverable
headings.reviewNote: Bars plaintiff from recovering special damages satisfied prior to trial by defendant or defendant's insurer.

headings.title: Credit and deduction of pre-trial special damage payments from judgment
headings.reviewNote: Entitles defendants to deduct pre-trial special damage payments from final judgments under section 490.710.

headings.title: Admissibility of evidence for other proper independent purposes
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section does not require exclusion of collateral evidence admissible for other proper purposes.

headings.title: Actual cost of medical care evidence and definition of financial obligation
headings.reviewNote: Permits evidence of actual medical costs, defining costs as paid amounts plus amounts owed after contractual discounts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections and section 538.305 cross-reference governing collateral source rule exclusivity, pre-trial payments, credits, and actual cost of medical care.

headings.title: Definition of wrongful taking in criminal property offenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines wrongful taking to include stealing, robbery, burglary, tampering, and property damage offenses.

headings.title: Admissibility of property photographs and required officer affidavits
headings.reviewNote: Makes signed photographs with owner placards and officer affidavits competent evidence in lieu of physical property.

headings.title: Return of photographed personal property to merchant or owner
headings.reviewNote: Requires return of physical property to merchant or owner upon filing photographs and affidavits with police or court.

headings.title: Applicability dates for property photography and purchasing affidavit rules
headings.reviewNote: Applies photography rules to prosecutions after August 13, 1988, and purchasing affidavits after August 28, 1993.

headings.title: Preservation of common law and statutory evidentiary admissibility
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section does not render inadmissible evidence otherwise admissible under statute or common law.

headings.title: Preliminary hearing retail value affidavits and trial testimony requirement
headings.reviewNote: Allows purchasing department affidavits on value at preliminary hearings, barring substitution for trial testimony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections on wrongful-taking property photographs, officer affidavits, property return, applicability dates, and preliminary hearing retail value affidavits.

headings.title: Definition of hazardous materials and controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Defines hazardous materials posing unreasonable risk, including controlled substances, explosives, and chemicals.

headings.title: Sampling and court-approved destruction of seized hazardous materials
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement with court approval to take representative samples and destroy remaining hazardous substances.

headings.title: Admissibility of representative samples, photographs, and lab reports
headings.reviewNote: Deems representative samples, photographs, and laboratory reports competent evidence in lieu of physical materials.

headings.title: Destruction of excess controlled substances and evidence retention rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires retaining only quantity necessary to prove offense weight elements, permitting destruction of excess.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections defining hazardous materials and governing court-approved sampling/destruction, sample/photo/lab admissibility, and excess controlled substance disposal.
